title: Uphill battle: Gadi Eisenkot's 3 paths to forming Israel's next government
gist: After Israel's Oct. 28, 2026 election, all opposition parties recommended Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot (67 of 120 Knesset seats) over Netanyahu (46), yet Israeli political sources say each of his three coalition paths is virtually unfeasible.

insights.claim: All Israeli opposition parties—Yashar, Together, Yisrael Beiteinu, The Democrats, the Arab Joint List and Raam—recommended Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government, giving him 67 of the Knesset's 120 members, above the 61-seat threshold.
insights.speaker: Rina Bassist
insights.so_what: Netanyahu has lost his majority on paper; a post-Netanyahu government is a real possibility for Israeli assets.
insights.quote: That gives him the backing of 67 of the Knesset’s 120 members, above the 61-seat majority threshold.

insights.claim: All but one coalition party recommended Benjamin Netanyahu—Likud, Religious Zionism/Zehut, Jewish Power and Shas—giving him the support of only 46 lawmakers.
insights.speaker: Rina Bassist
insights.so_what: One coalition party withholding support for Netanyahu signals cracks in the right-religious bloc.
insights.locator: All but one of the coalition

insights.claim: Israeli political sources say each of Eisenkot's three options for building a coalition is fraught with obstacles that make it virtually unfeasible, despite his 67 recommendations.
insights.speaker: Rina Bassist
insights.so_what: A 67-seat recommendation bloc that includes Arab parties and right-wing Yisrael Beiteinu may not translate into a governing coalition—prolonged deadlock or new elections are plausible.
insights.quote: each fraught with obstacles that make it virtually unfeasible

insights.claim: President Isaac Herzog held consultations with party representatives on who is best placed to form a stable government and was set to announce his choice on Sunday.
insights.speaker: Rina Bassist
insights.so_what: Herzog's mandate decision starts the coalition clock; watch for the formation deadline.
insights.locator: Herzog held consultations Wednesday and Thursday
